title: Geopolitics: Hormuz tensions keep negotiation and rerouting in focus
summary: A short edition: one geopolitical development had enough cross-source coverage for publication. Reporting described continued disagreement over the Strait of Hormuz alongside Iran's effort to shift some trade toward the Caspian route; GDELT and ISW feeds failed, and ReliefWeb returned no items.

stories.headline: Iranian minister says only negotiation can end conflict after Trump rejects Hormuz deal
stories.dek: Iran's public position on negotiations coincides with reporting on efforts to move trade north as the Strait of Hormuz remains impaired.
tldr: The BBC reported that Iran's foreign minister said negotiation was the only way to end the conflict after Trump rejected a Hormuz proposal.
DW separately reported that Iran maintained its position on the strait after the rejection.
Al Jazeera reported that Iran is shifting some trade north toward the Caspian Sea as the war affects the Hormuz route.

body.text: The BBC reported that Iran's foreign minister said only negotiation could end the conflict after Trump rejected a proposal concerning the Strait of Hormuz. DW's separate report also described Iran as sticking to its Hormuz position after the rejection.

Al Jazeera reported that Iran is shifting trade north toward the Caspian Sea as the war impairs the Strait of Hormuz. The coverage points to a potential rerouting response; it does not establish the scale or durability of that shift.

stories.whyItMatters: The strait is a strategic shipping corridor, so the dispute links diplomatic terms to the resilience of regional trade routes. Evidence of a northward shift is still reporting about an adjustment, not proof that it can replace the Hormuz route.
stories.editorNote: This story attributes the diplomatic position and trade rerouting to the named outlets. No unsupported shipping volumes, timelines or forecasts are added.
